finish.summary: I built a small two-storey shelf unit with two drawers and books on top. It's marked as a compromise because nothing here can check the 50 kg rating. The bottom storey is three bases in a row. The outer two are half bases, and each has a drawer on its cut face. A second storey of three bases is snapped on above, and the top is closed with covers. All open faces have end caps and the joints are bolted. A row of books stands across two of the top covers, and a stack of books sits on the third. The build check found no rule errors and no mesh clashes. The build has 57 parts, which is more than the usual 40 or so; most of the extra are snaps, caps and bolts. I can't confirm the 50 kg rating. The configurator only checks how parts fit, not how much load they take. The real strength depends on the plastic you print in and the print settings.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
